questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common oxidation state of lanthanides?
questions.solution: Lanthanides commonly exhibit a +3 oxidation state because they tend to lose two electrons from the 6s orbital and one electron from the 5d orbital, resulting in a stable +3 charge. Other oxidation states like +1, +2, or +4 are less common due to the stability of the +3 configuration. This makes +3 the most typical oxidation state for these elements.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an alloy formed by mixing transition metals?
questions.solution: Stainless steel is an alloy formed by mixing transition metals like chromium, vanadium, tungsten, molybdenum, and manganese with iron. Brass and bronze are alloys of transition metals with non-transition metals, while copper is a pure metal, not an alloy.

questions.solution: The lanthanoid contraction occurs because the 4f electrons do not shield each other effectively from the increasing nuclear charge, causing the atomic radius to decrease. Perfect shielding would prevent this effect, so it is incorrect. An increase in nuclear charge alone does not account for the contraction, and a decrease in atomic number is unrelated to the phenomenon.

questions.stem: Why do transition metals have high enthalpies of atomisation?
choices: Because they have completely filled d orbitals
Because they have a large number of unpaired electrons
Because they have a low number of valence electrons
Because they are not metallic in nature
questions.solution: The correct answer is because they have a large number of unpaired electrons, which contribute to strong metallic bonding and high enthalpies of atomisation. Completely filled d orbitals would result in weaker bonding, a low number of valence electrons would not support strong interactions, and not being metallic contradicts the nature of transition metals.

questions.stem: Why does zinc have a lower enthalpy of atomisation compared to other elements in the 3d series?
choices: It has a stable d^10 configuration
It has a higher nuclear charge
It has a lower atomic radius
questions.solution: Zinc has a lower enthalpy of atomisation because its d-orbitals are completely filled, giving it a stable d^10 configuration, which reduces the energy needed to separate its atoms. A higher nuclear charge would increase the attraction between the nucleus and electrons, making atomisation harder. More unpaired electrons would generally lead to stronger metallic bonding and higher enthalpy of atomisation. A lower atomic radius would also increase the strength of metallic bonds, not decrease them.

questions.stem: What is the effect of lanthanoid contraction on the properties of transition elements?
choices: It increases the atomic radii of the third d series
It decreases the density of the transition elements
It causes the third d series to have similar properties to the second d series
It increases the number of unpaired electrons in the third d series
questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction refers to the decrease in atomic size of the lanthanoid elements, which results in the third d series having similar properties to the second d series due to comparable atomic radii. The other options are incorrect because atomic radii do not increase, density is not necessarily decreased, and the number of unpaired electrons is not directly affected by lanthanoid contraction.

mr.solution: लॅन्थेनॉइड अपक्षय हा लॅन्थेनॉइड घटकांच्या परमाणू आकारात घट होण्याचा अर्थ आहे, जे तिसऱ्या डी श्रेणीला दुसऱ्या डी श्रेणीसारखे गुणधर्म देते कारण त्यांच्या परमाणू त्रिज्या तुलनात्मक असतात. इतर विकल्प अयोग्य आहेत कारण परमाणू त्रिज्या वाढत नाही, घनता निश्चितपणे कमी होत नाही आणि अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉनची संख्या लॅन्थेनॉइड अपक्षयामुळे प्रत्यक्षपणे प्रभावित होत नाही.
